opening.argument: Two people sit across a table with microphones while the speaker describes how they invested their own capital in index funds and starting companies. The Ethereum discussion likewise concerns a personal holding: the speaker says the position is long-standing, reports that it has done well, and explains the observation about developer activity that informed it. A reported past result, even one that remained positive despite a decline, is not a promise of future returns. Nothing in the supplied discussion establishes a required payment or asks viewers to act. The financial material is an interview-style account of personal investment decisions, not a concrete offer to the audience.

citations.quote: I invested all of my available capital into index funds, outside of investing in starting companies.
I have a very long standing, large position in Ethereum
which I've held for like six years or something, which has done me very well.
I could see that developers are building on top of Ethereum more than any other blockchain. So that insight was really beneficial to me.
